name: Toronto
intro: Toronto and GTA lots are tight, so the courts that fit here are usually 25 by 20 or 30 by 25 half courts that share the yard with a patio or a pool.
local: In the 416 and the inner suburbs, the first question is what fits. A 25 by 20 foot half court works on many detached lots and doubles as a hard-surface play area. In Vaughan, Oakville, Aurora and King, larger lots make room for a 30 by 60 multi-sport pad.
Kits ship by freight to anywhere in the GTA. If your street is narrow or your driveway is short, tell us and we will ask for a smaller truck with a liftgate.
Southern Ontario freeze-thaw cycles are hard on painted concrete. Tiles float on top of the pad, so the playing surface is not affected by the hairline cracks most slabs develop over time.

name: Ottawa
intro: Ottawa winters are long and the frost goes deep. A tile court over a well-built pad is ready to play as soon as the snow is gone.
local: Suburban lots in Kanata, Barrhaven and Orleans generally suit a 30 by 25 basketball half court or a 52 by 28 pickleball court. Rural properties in Greely, Manotick and Carp have room for a full 30 by 60 multi-sport pad.
Because the surface is perforated, meltwater drains through instead of sitting on top. Courts dry quickly in spring and after summer storms.
We quote freight to the whole National Capital Region, including Gatineau and the Outaouais side.

name: Calgary
intro: Calgary is one of the sunniest cities in Canada, with chinooks that can swing the temperature in an afternoon. Outdoor sport tile is made for that kind of weather.
local: Acreages in Springbank, Bearspaw and De Winton have the room for full courts and 30 by 60 multi-sport pads. In the city, a 30 by 25 half court beside the garage is the natural fit.
Big temperature swings make any plastic surface expand and contract. Leaving a small perimeter gap, which we show on the layout plan, lets the court move without buckling.
Kits are quoted with freight to Calgary, Airdrie, Cochrane, Okotoks and the surrounding rural addresses.

name: Vancouver
intro: On the wet coast, a court that drains is the difference between playing in November and waiting for July. Open-grid tiles shed rain straight through.
local: In the Lower Mainland the room for a court is mostly found in the Fraser Valley, Langley, Surrey and on the North Shore. Pickleball has grown quickly here, and a 52 by 28 kit fits where a tennis court never would.
Painted concrete gets slick with moss and standing water in a coastal winter. A perforated tile surface keeps water moving off the top so the court is playable sooner after rain.
We quote freight to Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley and Vancouver Island. Island deliveries are quoted to your door, ferry included.

name: Edmonton
intro: Edmonton summers are short and the evenings are long. A backyard court can be in use from after school until the sun goes down at ten.
local: Acreages in Sherwood Park, St. Albert, Spruce Grove and Leduc County can fit a 30 by 60 pad with room to spare. In town, a half court on the garage pad is the simplest project.
Tiles stay outside all winter. Clear them with a blower or a plastic shovel and the court is ready on the first warm day.
Freight quotes cover Edmonton and the capital region. Ask for liftgate service if the delivery is to a residential driveway.
